paper.title: Machine learning techniques for identification of carcinogenic mutations, which cause breast adenocarcinoma

task.problem_type: Binary classification of gene mutations into carcinogenic driver mutations vs normal/passenger mutations for breast adenocarcinoma identification
task.goal: Use machine learning on engineered genomic-sequence features to identify carcinogenic mutations associated with breast adenocarcinoma

dataset.construction_method: The paper states that IntOGen provides mutation information but not mutated sequences, so the authors developed a Python application to inject mutation information into normal gene sequences to construct mutated sequences.

class_definition.positive_class: Driver mutations / mutated gene sequences causing cancer
class_definition.negative_class: Normal gene sequences; passenger mutations are treated as non-carcinogenic and considered normal sequences

not_reported: Exact train/test counts for each split

pipeline: Construct mutated sequences using a custom Python application
Extract handcrafted features from gene sequences

imbalance_handling.description: Minority class oversampling through interpolation between a selected minority sample and its neighbors
steps_reported: Randomly choose minority instance K and its neighbors N
Compute difference between N and K
Multiply difference by a random value between 0 and 1 and add to K
Repeat until desired synthetic samples are generated
not_reported: Whether SMOTE was applied before or within each fold

feature_scaling.details: Paper explicitly states that feature scaling allows each data sample to participate in detection, but it does not specify the scaler type.
not_reported: Whether fit was done per train fold only

missing_data_handling.details: The paper states that raw moments are used for data imputation.
not_reported: Whether imputation was actually needed on the final feature table

reported_features: Hahn moments / Hahne's polynomial based features
RAAPIV (Reverse Accumulative Absolute Position Incidence Vector)
notes: PRIM is described as a 20 x 20 matrix.
RPRIM is the reverse-sequence analogue of PRIM.
AAPIV/RAAPIV encode composition and relative positioning information.
The paper presents equations for several feature families but does not clearly specify the final concatenated feature dimension used for classification.
replication_gaps: No explicit final feature vector length
No exact encoding scheme for nucleotide/gene symbols into matrices/vectors
No full algorithmic pseudocode for feature extraction
No software package or code repository

DecisionTree.description: Supervised tree-based classifier using entropy and information gain

GaussianNaiveBayes.description: Probabilistic classifier based on Bayes theorem with Gaussian assumptions

RandomForest.description: Ensemble of decision trees; results merged/averaged for prediction

tenfold_cv.description: Data is equally partitioned into 10 groups; each group is used once for validation and the results are averaged

auc_roc.note: ROC curves and fold-level ROC areas are shown, but a single tabulated AUC value per classifier/evaluation setup is generally not reported except as values visible in ROC plots.

not_reported: Recall as a separate tabulated metric

DecisionTree.auc_or_roc_note: ROC described as between 0.99 and 1.0; visually near-perfect

auc_precision_recall_f1_summary.recall: Not explicitly reported as recall; sensitivity is reported and can be treated as recall in binary classification

minimum_reproducible_pipeline_from_paper: Collect normal breast-adenocarcinoma-related gene sequences from Ensembl.
Collect driver/passenger mutation information from IntOGen for 99 genes.
Construct mutated sequences by injecting mutation metadata into normal sequences using custom code.
Label driver mutations as positive/carcinogenic and normal plus passenger mutations as negative/non-carcinogenic.
Extract handcrafted sequence features including Hahn moments, raw/central moments, PRIM, RPRIM, frequency matrix, AAPIV, and RAAPIV.
Train Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and Random Forest classifiers.
Evaluate with self-consistency test, 80/20 independent test split, and 10-fold cross-validation.
Report accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, MCC, and ROC/AUC.

major_missing_details: No exact feature vector construction pipeline
No exact dimensionality of the final features
No train/test sample counts after balancing
important_caveats: Some reported MCC values appear unusual relative to the very high accuracies, especially in self-consistency and independent testing.
ROC/AUC values are mostly inferred from text and plots rather than presented as a clean result table.
The paper is more reproducible at the high-level workflow stage than at the exact implementation stage.
replication_gaps_and_warnings.replication_risk: High for exact reproduction, moderate for approximate reproduction of the overall workflow
